forecasts.label: Capital financing requirement
forecasts.note: Restated at each quarterly return. The Q4 restatement comes from the annual return itself, so it lands on the outturn by construction — the interesting movement is Q1 to Q3.

forecasts.label: Interest payable
forecasts.note: The council's own full-year forecast, restated at each quarterly return.

forecasts.label: Revenue spending (net current expenditure)
forecasts.note: The full-year forecast of net current expenditure — the running cost of services — restated each quarter against the same measure at outturn.

forecasts.label: Capital expenditure
forecasts.note: Total capital spending forecast each quarter (the capital payments return) against the annual capital outturn. Capital spending not met from grants or receipts is what turns into new borrowing, so a forecast running ahead of outturn is a borrowing signal.

in_year.label: Interest payable, as reported each quarter
in_year.note: Per quarter, not cumulative. The quarterly return is a lighter collection than the annual one and sums to roughly 92% of it nationally, so the two are shown apart rather than added together.

findings.headline: Investment property portfolio yielding 5.62%, above 5% target; tenant recovered from CVA
findings.detail: The council's property investment portfolio (£20m allocated in 2017 with 5% return target) comprises four properties valued at £17.255m generating £1.049m forecast rental income, achieving 5.62% average yield. Norwich property performing particularly well at 7.83% yield. Nottingham property's tenant (Robinson Webster/Jigsaw Ltd) has recovered from Company Voluntary Agreement: rent has been restored from concessionary rate of £12,000 pa to market rent of £60,369 pa following CVA end on 8 April 2023.
findings.matters: Investment strategy is delivering returns above target. Tenant recovery represents improvement in underlying asset quality and rental resilience.
findings.figures: Total portfolio value £17.255m; forecast rental £1.049m (average yield 5.62% vs 5% target); Norwich 7.83% (£561k rent), Lincoln Drive 5.04% (£138k rent), South Oxhey Maisonettes 5.04% (£145k rent), Nottingham 4.59% (£205k rent); Jigsaw rent recovered from £12,000 pa to £60,369 pa
findings.quote: The total rent due is forecast to be £1.049m which will achieve an average yield of 5.62%, above the 5% target.

findings.headline: Aquadrome Bridge remedial works approved by urgent decision; £260k capital increase
findings.detail: Remedial works to Aquadrome Bridge were approved via urgent decision dated 25 February 2026, adding £260k to the capital budget. This is one of the material capital variances reported in Period 3.
findings.matters: Unplanned remedial works indicate asset condition issue requiring urgent spend. Urgent decision process suggests time-critical nature that could not be deferred.
findings.quote: Increase in budget for remedial works to the bridge was agreed by urgent decision 25/2/26

findings.headline: Capital programme carries forward £14.831m from 2025/26; two-thirds of current budget is prior-year spend
findings.detail: The original 2026/27 capital budget was £6.795m, but latest budget of £22.129m includes £14.831m rephased from 2025/26, meaning 67% of current budget is prior-year carry-forward. This indicates delivery timing issues in the prior year. Spend to date at Period 3 is only £2.735m (12.36% of total budget), suggesting back-loaded delivery through the remainder of the year.
findings.matters: Large carry-forward indicates capital delivery variability in prior year. Low early-year spend rate signals potential for further slippage, though existing rephasing provides some cushion.
findings.figures: Original budget £6.795m; rephasing £14.831m; latest budget £22.129m; spend to date £2.735m (12.36% of budget)
findings.quote: The latest budget which totals £22.129m for 2026/27 includes the variances previously reported to Policy & Resources Committee in March 2026 (Period 10 Budget Monitoring) and approved at Council 14 July 2026 (2025/26 year end report). The forecast Year end position for 2026/27 is estimated to be £22.406m, which reflects rephasing of £14.831m from 2025/26.

findings.headline: Recycling disposal now costs the council; global demand decline expected to persist
findings.detail: The council's recycling disposal contract is variable and linked to global commodities markets. With reduced global demand for recyclable materials, the council now faces disposal costs rather than generating income. China's economy appears to have entered recession, suggesting weak demand for recyclable materials will persist. The council is forecasting conservatively, assuming no recovery in recyclable income.
findings.matters: This represents an operating cost exposure varying with global commodity markets beyond the council's control. Conservative forecast means near-term outlook is for continued disposal costs.
findings.figures: Specific cost figures not disclosed; reflected in budget variances
findings.quote: Currently, the Council faces a cost to dispose of recycling as demand for materials has reduced. Recent economic performance data released from China, where the economy appears to have entered a recession, suggests that demand for recyclable materials could remain low for longer, increasing the cost to the Council.

findings.headline: Council Tax and Business Rates collections declining year-on-year despite being ahead of cash-flow profile
findings.detail: At 30 June 2026, Council Tax collection stands at 30.2% (5.69 percentage points ahead of the 24.51% monthly profile target) but is 0.1 percentage point behind the prior-year position of 30.3%. Business Rates collection is at 30.87% (6.12 percentage points ahead of 24.75% profile) but down 0.76 percentage points year-on-year from 31.63%. The council warns that cost of living crisis and recession risks will continue affecting collection, with impacts feeding through the Collection Fund to affect 2027/28 spending power.
findings.matters: Declining year-on-year collection rates despite ahead-of-profile cash position signal underlying household and business cash pressures. Collection Fund deficits affect the following year's available spending power.
findings.figures: Council Tax 30.2% collected (5.69pp ahead of profile); down 0.1pp year-on-year. Business Rates 30.87% (6.12pp ahead of profile); down 0.76pp year-on-year
findings.quote: Year on year, the collection of Council Tax is marginally behind of the position reported at 30 June 2025 when 30.3% (-0.1%) of Council Tax due had been collected and Business Rates is also behind when 31.63% (-0.76%) of Business Rates due had been collected.
